newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam sentences Canadian to death for drug crime.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam sentences Canadian to death for drug crime.

text.p: A Canadian national was sentenced to death and her Vietnamese mother was given a life prison sentence by a Hanoi court on Monday for trafficking heroin, court officials and a Canadian diplomat said.

The diplomat said that Nguyen Thi Hiep of Montreal and Tran Thi Cam, who were arrested last April at Hanoi airport as they checked in for a flight to Hong Kong, had 15 days to appeal against the ruling.

The diplomat said that the court, which was not open to foreign journalists during the trial, also fined the 40-year-old Canadian woman one billion dong ($86,000) and her 70-year-old mother 500 million dong.
He said they were charged with attempting to take 5.45 kg (12 lb) of heroin out of the country. Under Vietnamese law, trafficking in as little as one kg (2.2 lb) of heroin is punishable by death.
The diplomat said Hiep, who was reported by local newspapers to have left Vietnam in 1982 and gained Canadian nationality in 1985, was still considered a Vietnamese citizen by Hanoi.

There are currently six Canadians, including Hiep, being detained in Vietnam, mostly for offences arising from business disputes. The diplomat said Canada was urgently seeking consular access to Hiep following the sentence.
